experiment: adaptive prompt injection vs out-of-band action detection (AgentDojo workspace)

firm_results.monitor_utility_cost: zero — 15/15 benign tasks solved with the monitor attached
firm_results.static_attack_success_rate: 0.0 across all six AgentDojo attack families
firm_results.adaptive_attack_success_rate_observed: 0.0 within a 3-5 iteration budget on model-router

honest_reading: A current frontier model (behind Azure model-router) resists BOTH the static AgentDojo attacks and a black-box adaptive attacker within a modest budget. The model itself is the strong defense. Consequently the detection-asymmetry comparison cannot yet be measured on this target: there are no successful attacks to score either detector on.
what_this_needs_to_become_a_measurement: a weaker/older target model (AgentDojo supports GPT-3.5-class targets) where attacks land, OR
a much larger attacker budget and stronger jailbroken attacker model, OR
a longer-horizon multi-step injection task where the malicious action blends into normal tool patterns
why_the_negative_result_is_still_useful: It is a current, dated, reproducible data point that static injection benchmarks are saturated on 2026 frontier models, matching the adaptive-attack literature's warning, and it establishes the zero-utility-cost property of out-of-band monitoring cleanly.
